verses.text: If thou wilt make any progress keep thyself in the fear of God, and long not to be too free, but restrain all thy senses under discipline and give not thyself up to senseless mirth.
verses.modernizedText: If you want to make any progress, keep yourself in the fear of God and do not long to be too free, but restrain all your senses under discipline and do not give yourself up to senseless mirth.

verses.text: Give thyself to compunction of heart and thou shalt find devotion.
verses.modernizedText: Give yourself to compunction of heart, and you will find devotion.

verses.text: Compunction openeth the way for many good things, which dissoluteness is wont quickly to lose.
verses.modernizedText: Compunction opens the way for many good things that dissipation is accustomed to lose quickly.

verses.text: It is wonderful that any man can ever rejoice heartily in this life who considereth and weigheth his banishment, and the manifold dangers which beset his soul.
verses.modernizedText: It is remarkable that anyone can ever rejoice heartily in this life who considers and weighs his banishment and the many dangers that beset his soul.

verses.text: Through lightness of heart and neglect of our shortcomings we feel not the sorrows of our soul, but often vainly laugh when we have good cause to weep.
verses.modernizedText: Through lightness of heart and neglect of our shortcomings, we do not feel the sorrows of our soul, but often laugh vainly when we have good cause to weep.

verses.text: There is no true liberty nor real joy, save in the fear of God with a good conscience.
verses.modernizedText: There is no true liberty or real joy except in the fear of God with a good conscience.

verses.text: Happy is he who can cast away every cause of distraction and bring himself to the one purpose of holy compunction.
verses.modernizedText: Happy is the person who can cast away every cause of distraction and bring himself to the one purpose of holy compunction.

verses.text: Happy is he who putteth away from him whatsoever may stain or burden his conscience.
verses.modernizedText: Happy is the person who puts away whatever may stain or burden his conscience.

verses.text: Strive manfully; custom is overcome by custom.
verses.modernizedText: Strive courageously; habit is overcome by habit.

verses.text: If thou knowest how to let men alone, they will gladly let thee alone to do thine own works.
verses.modernizedText: If you know how to leave others alone, they will gladly leave you alone to do your own work.

verses.text: Busy not thyself with the affairs of others, nor entangle thyself with the business of great men.
verses.modernizedText: Do not busy yourself with the affairs of others or entangle yourself in the business of great people.

verses.text: Keep always thine eye upon thyself first of all, and give advice to thyself specially before all thy dearest friends.
verses.modernizedText: Always keep your eye first of all on yourself, and give advice especially to yourself before all your dearest friends.

verses.text: If thou hast not the favour of men, be not thereby cast down, but let thy concern be that thou holdest not thyself so well and circumspectly, as becometh a servant of God and a devout monk.
verses.modernizedText: If you do not have the favor of others, do not be cast down by it, but let your concern be that you do not conduct yourself as well and as carefully as befits a servant of God and a devout monk.

verses.text: It is often better and safer for a man not to have many comforts in this life, especially those which concern the flesh.
verses.modernizedText: It is often better and safer for a person not to have many comforts in this life, especially those concerning the flesh.

verses.text: But that we lack divine comforts or feel them rarely is to our own blame, because we seek not compunction of heart, nor utterly cast away those comforts which are vain and worldly.
verses.modernizedText: But it is our own fault that we lack divine comforts or feel them rarely, because we do not seek compunction of heart or utterly cast away those comforts that are vain and worldly.

verses.text: Know thyself to be unworthy of divine consolation, and worthy rather of much tribulation.
verses.modernizedText: Know yourself to be unworthy of divine consolation and worthy instead of much tribulation.

verses.text: When a man hath perfect compunction, then all the world is burdensome and bitter to him.
verses.modernizedText: When a person has perfect compunction, then all the world is burdensome and bitter to him.

verses.text: A good man will find sufficient cause for mourning and weeping; for whether he considereth himself, or pondereth concerning his neighbour, he knoweth that no man liveth here without tribulation, and the more thoroughly he considereth himself, the more thoroughly he grieveth.
verses.modernizedText: A good person will find sufficient cause for mourning and weeping; for whether he considers himself or ponders his neighbor, he knows that no one lives here without tribulation, and the more thoroughly he considers himself, the more thoroughly he grieves.

verses.text: Grounds for just grief and inward compunction there are in our sins and vices, wherein we lie so entangled that we are but seldom able to contemplate heavenly things.
verses.modernizedText: There are grounds for just grief and inward compunction in our sins and vices, in which we lie so entangled that we are only seldom able to contemplate heavenly things.

verses.text: If thou thoughtest upon thy death more often than how long thy life should be, thou wouldest doubtless strive more earnestly to improve.
verses.modernizedText: If you thought about your death more often than about how long your life would be, you would doubtless strive more earnestly to improve.

verses.text: And if thou didst seriously consider the future pains of hell, I believe thou wouldest willingly endure toil or pain and fear not discipline.
verses.modernizedText: And if you seriously considered the future pains of hell, I believe you would willingly endure toil or pain and not fear discipline.

verses.text: But because these things reach not the heart, and we still love pleasant things, therefore we remain cold and miserably indifferent.
verses.modernizedText: But because these things do not reach the heart and we still love pleasant things, we remain cold and miserably indifferent.

verses.text: Oftentimes it is from poverty of spirit that the wretched body is so easily led to complain.
verses.modernizedText: Often it is from poverty of spirit that the wretched body is so easily led to complain.

verses.text: Pray therefore humbly unto the Lord that He will give thee the spirit of compunction and say in the language of the prophet, Feed me, O Lord, with bread of tears, and give me plenteousness of tears to drink.(1)
verses.modernizedText: Therefore, pray humbly to the Lord that He will give you the spirit of compunction, and say in the language of the prophet, Feed me, O Lord, with bread of tears, and give me plenty of tears to drink.(1)
